title: Luckread Cloudflare D1 to PostgreSQL Portability Contract
purpose: Keep the Luckread application data model Cloudflare D1-native today while preserving a low-cost, deterministic migration path to PostgreSQL providers such as GCP Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL or other PostgreSQL-compatible services later.

authority.sourceOfTruth: This contract is subordinate to the official Payload adapter contracts and is authoritative for Luckread-owned application data design.
authority.principle: Portability is achieved through a portable logical domain model, not by pretending D1 and PostgreSQL have identical physical capabilities.

architecture.adapterBoundary: Database-specific SQL, types, connection handling, indexes, migrations, and extensions must remain below the application data contract boundary.

nonNegotiableInvariants: Application APIs and domain state machines must not expose D1-specific physical types or table implementation details.
Application-owned identifiers must remain opaque and portable across D1 and PostgreSQL.
Application-owned timestamps must have an explicit logical UTC contract independent of physical timestamp type.
Business enums and state machines must be represented by stable application values, not vendor enum types.
Business JSON must have a logical JSON contract; D1 may serialize it as TEXT while PostgreSQL may use JSONB only as an implementation optimization after portability review.
Application logic must not depend on SQLite rowid, PostgreSQL serial sequences, or any other vendor-generated identity mechanism.
Application logic must not depend on PostgreSQL-only functions, extensions, stored procedures, or triggers unless a portable fallback contract exists.
Application-owned tables must be migratable without depending on Payload internal table names or undocumented adapter internals.
R2/object storage references must remain storage-provider-neutral at the domain level even when Cloudflare R2 is the initial implementation.
Cache, KV, queue, and object-storage bindings must never become part of the authoritative relational domain contract.

portableLogicalTypes.id: Opaque TEXT logical identifier; may map to PostgreSQL text/uuid only through an explicit migration mapping without changing API identity semantics.
portableLogicalTypes.integer: Signed integer logical value; physical range must remain within both D1/SQLite and target PostgreSQL contract limits.
portableLogicalTypes.boolean: Logical boolean; D1 implementation INTEGER 0/1, PostgreSQL implementation may use boolean.
portableLogicalTypes.decimal: Use only where required and define precision/scale in the logical contract; do not assume SQLite REAL is sufficient for financial values.
portableLogicalTypes.timestamp: UTC instant with millisecond logical precision; D1 implementation INTEGER epoch milliseconds; PostgreSQL implementation may use timestamptz with an explicit conversion boundary.
portableLogicalTypes.json: Logical JSON document with bounded size and canonical serialization rules; physical representation is adapter-specific.
portableLogicalTypes.text: UTF-8 application text with explicit length/semantic constraints at the application contract level.
portableLogicalTypes.binary: Opaque binary data should normally be object storage, not relational storage; BLOB/bytea is reserved for genuinely small binary values.

schemaRules.portablePrimaryKey: Use stable application IDs rather than database-generated row identity as the domain key.
schemaRules.foreignKeys: Foreign-key relationships must be expressible in both SQLite/D1 and PostgreSQL; application integrity must not rely solely on vendor-specific constraint behavior.
schemaRules.indexes: Define logical access patterns first. Physical index definitions may differ between D1 and PostgreSQL and must be adapter-specific.
schemaRules.uniqueConstraints: Business uniqueness rules must be explicitly documented and portable; collation-sensitive uniqueness must declare its normalization strategy.
schemaRules.checks: CHECK constraints may be used where supported by both targets, but state-machine validation remains an application contract as well.
schemaRules.nullable: Nullability is part of the logical schema and must not be inferred from adapter defaults.
schemaRules.naming: Application table and column names must use stable domain terminology and must not encode database vendor semantics.

mustNotLeakIntoDomain: Cloudflare-specific KV keys as relational identifiers

allowedPhysicalOptimizations: JSONB for bounded application JSON where query patterns justify it
PostgreSQL-specific index types after workload validation
forbiddenMigrationShortcuts: Changing public IDs solely to match PostgreSQL native types
Changing API field names because PostgreSQL uses different physical names
Rewriting application state machines around PostgreSQL enums
Moving authoritative application state into PostgreSQL-specific extensions without a contract
Making PostgreSQL JSONB semantics part of the public API
Making stored procedures the only implementation of critical business rules
postgresMigrationRules.migrationRequirement: A D1-to-PostgreSQL migration must be a physical storage migration behind the same logical application contract, not an API/domain rewrite.

r2AndStoragePortability.rule: The logical object reference must not require Cloudflare R2 semantics. A future GCP deployment may map the same contract to Google Cloud Storage without changing the domain API.
r2AndStoragePortability.migration: Object data may be copied independently from relational migration; D1/PostgreSQL records remain metadata and integrity references.

migrationPhases: Freeze logical schema and API contracts
Export D1 application-owned records in canonical logical format
Create PostgreSQL physical schema from the logical contract
Reconcile counts, hashes, uniqueness, foreign-key relationships, and state-machine validity
Migrate object storage references and validate object integrity
Run dual-read or shadow validation where required
Cut over authoritative writes only after reconciliation passes
Keep rollback path until post-cutover verification completes
verificationRequirements: API contract compatibility test before and after physical database substitution
failClosedConditions: A domain field cannot be represented without a D1-to-PostgreSQL conversion rule
A public API field depends on a vendor-specific physical type
A migration requires changing stable application identifiers without an explicit versioned contract
A business rule exists only as a PostgreSQL-specific implementation with no application-level contract
A D1-only implementation leaks binding names or SQLite semantics into domain APIs
A PostgreSQL migration requires rewriting Payload/Luckread API contracts merely to preserve database compatibility
designDirective: Design for D1 now, but treat PostgreSQL as a first-class future physical target. Cloudflare optimization must reduce cost and improve runtime fit without creating irreversible domain-model or API coupling.
